note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following biopsy-proven high-grade prostate cancer with rising PSA.

Recently retired plumber, 69 years of age, presents for urological re-evaluation. Medical history is significant for hypercholesterolaemia, managed with atorvastatin, and known COPD with recent pulmonary function testing. The patient is a current smoker with a 35 pack-year history. PSA levels have risen progressively from 2.5 ng/mL in June 2023 to 10.92 ng/mL in January 2025. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 12/35. Socially, he lives in a ground-floor apartment with his partner, consumes 9 units of alcohol weekly, and performs light weight-training twice a week. Recent unrelated appointments include cataract review in ophthalmology and a surveillance colonoscopy in gastroenterology.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable with no discrete nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.
